title: Coordinate-Free Cyclic Vector: Single Operator and PID Modules

problemStatement.formal: \text{Let } V \text{ be a finite-dimensional } K\text{-vector space and } T : V \to V \text{ linear. Then } T \text{ is nonderogatory (}\min\text{poly} = \text{char poly}) \iff T \text{ admits a cyclic vector } v \text{ (i.e. } \{v, Tv, T^2v, \dots\} \text{ spans } V\text{).}
problemStatement.plain: The parent gallery proof shows, for matrices over any field, that a matrix is "nonderogatory" (its minimal and characteristic polynomials coincide) exactly when it has a cyclic vector — a single vector whose images under repeated application generate the whole space. This problem asks whether that matrix proof can be lifted to a coordinate-free statement about an abstract linear operator $T : V \to V$, and then recognized as an instance of the PID structure theorem by treating $V$ as a module over the polynomial ring $K[x]$ where $x$ acts as $T$. The payoff is connecting the entry to Mathlib's `Module` and PID-structure infrastructure instead of `Matrix`.
